claims.summary: Current browser auth uses token login and a signed HttpOnly cookie.
Production browser auth validates Access JWT signature and claims, derives verified-email principals and keeps Bearer automation separate.
Sessions, mutable Agent runtime state, Memory, vectors and persistent Desktop approvals are principal-scoped; owner retains the legacy data paths.
Ask performs no Memory or tool writes and all vector retrieval paths soft-degrade without hidden runtime initialization.
Plan may inspect through ToolGateway; write and exec capabilities are rejected.

Auto is a policy preset over the canonical AgentToolLoop and ToolGateway (RunBudget/RunPolicy from AutoBudgets). There is no separate Auto orchestration engine, no fabricated plan/shards, no planner/coders/merge labels, and no verifier PASSED without a real postcondition check.

Auto supplies an independent positive native-call cap to the existing ToolLoop/Gateway path. Each completed ToolResult, including failure or denial, consumes one call; ApprovalRequired does not. Captured continuation retains cap and executed prefix across resume; N+1 is blocked before Gateway/approval, while exactly N is not automatically budget failure. Iteration safety guard and verifier remain separate; uncapped callers retain prior semantics. Dispatch faults stop without replay and preserve available typed prefix, without asserting the unknown last effect. This is not strict wall-time, file/token accounting, durable recovery or new authority.

Auto fences new model generation, post-model acceptance, each native/approved call and verifier admission at the original finite monotonic expiry, including approval wait and exact >= boundary. Captured continuation retains expiry across new loop/env settings; cancellation precedes expiry at loop and pre-verifier boundaries, completed prefix survives budget stop. Already-running operations are not interrupted and a verifier admitted before expiry can finish later. Expiry-less callers, R1a quota and existing authorization remain; no hard deadline, file/token/retry accounting, persistence or durable recovery claim.

Auto projects the count of known unique published workspace_run and admitted direct-writer paths. Read-only calls and refusals that provably did not publish add no effects. Incomplete observation becomes null. Numeric projection retains explicit nonnegative counts and unknown while rejecting malformed values. Verifier effects and reconciliation remain outside this accounting contract.

Existing sync adapters and shared SSE decoder use one pure usage validator: all three explicit nonnegative integer (non-bool) counts produce LLMUsage, including explicit zero; missing, partial or invalid metadata becomes unknown None without discarding valid text/tool calls. Existing xAI input/output aliases and canonical precedence remain. Unknown emits no synthetic zero Usage event; complete updates remain separate. No inferred total, aggregation, quota, transport, capability, authority or billing verification change.

Auto retains the original staged workspace_run limit and unique published paths across approval. ToolGateway supplies trusted limits and the verified host-stage snapshot is checked before atomic exchange. A budget refusal with confirmed cleanup consumes no paths and allows retry; retained or unknown effects prevent further staged execution. Direct writers share this ledger and have a separate pre-admission check.

Managed Auto write, create, rename, move, delete and patch check unique prospective paths inside the mutation guard before the first write. A successful operation adds those paths to the same ledger as staged publication. A partial failure invalidates further file admission.

Sync Auto opts into immutable external Brain.generate usage accounting: started/reported/unknown calls and complete reported sums survive approval continuation and available stop/fault results. Synthetic resume is not another model request; received metadata precedes post-model cancellation/expiry. Numeric Auto-state projection rejects malformed summaries without synthesizing usage. Accounting alone does not stop execution; Auto token admission is a separate policy. Internal HTTP retries, other model consumers, stream aggregation, verifier usage, billing, quota and durable recovery are not covered; existing dispatch/approval/expiry/cap behavior remains.

Sync Auto gates only the next genuine Brain.generate on captured reported token limit: first request allowed, unknown usage blocks with an uncertainty reason, complete sum >= cap blocks as exhausted. Captured cap and accounting survive approvals/new loop/env; synthetic approved remainder and final verifier retain existing guards. Cancellation/expiry precede token admission; no automatic replay. Existing defaults/loader, non-Auto and streaming policy remain. This is not a hard spending/billing cap: active request overshoot, HTTP retries, other model consumers and verifier usage are not covered.
Deterministic Ask to Plan to Act orchestration is a target, not current Auto behavior.
Target architecture derives typed user-facing communication artifacts from authoritative lifecycle state through a communication decision layer; current streaming/UIHub paths are not this contract.

Target architecture accepts lifecycle completion only after policy-selected verification and acceptance for the exact task/result/artifact revision; current verifier paths are partial evidence mechanisms.

Target lifecycle contract separates terminal cause (completed/failed/cancelled/aborted) from result disposition (full/accepted_partial/none), treats supersession as status/lineage, and gives every accepted Ask a durable task identity with one semantic final; current runtime is not this contract.

Owner can save an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, then select a session model. Custom routes start Chat-only and members remain denied. Explicit owner/session confirm checks four inert sync/stream tool-call and role=tool requests without host actions or chat history. Transient Agent-owned evidence binds exact endpoint/model/effective headers/key and config/credential revisions; changed/revoked context and other sessions remain unqualified. No proof is persisted in ModelConfig. Existing ToolGateway policy remains mandatory. LocalHttpBrain native SSE is scoped/cancellable with no redirects/replay. Built-in legacy adapter admission is not model qualification; no production endpoint is claimed qualified by fixture tests.

Target SlavikAI provides a first-class user-selected subscription-backed OpenAI/ChatGPT access route distinct from API-key billing, with explicit entitlement, trust and non-silent fallback boundaries; no current runtime implementation is claimed.

Explicit Memory requests create a preview; only confirm or edit-and-confirm writes it, while reject performs no write. End-session first asks Yes/No/Cancel and prepares a summary only after Yes; a separate Memory confirmation is required before saving and closing.
The public API exposes and accepts only the exact proxy model id slavik; all other IDs are rejected before Agent resolution.
Desktop uses owner-scoped persistent approvals, one shared-host run lease, dispatch allowlisting and observable retryable rollback.
Manifest body instructions and supporting dependencies are resolved and injected per run into Auto preset; Response reporting observes the run without changing tool or verification authority.
A clean local PR branch can run preflight before it has an upstream.
The environment example uses a complete OpenAI-compatible chat completions URL.
Production background execution has separate venv-prod pid and log targets.
Sandbox process execution is unavailable under I0 before spawn. Existing process-result projection semantics remain defined, but no qualified generic Sandbox executor is shipped.
Complete scoped durable execution evidence precedes lossy projections; configurable seven-day terminal retention excludes active, resumable and recovery-pinned data.

Scoped durable admission identities, immutable revision/history and CAS transitions. UI Ask and Auto now admit and fence repeated dispatch after volatile replay loss using structured request fingerprints bound to grants, effective tools/policy and full execution config, with pre-admission history checked before dispatch. Existing admitted runs cannot be reclaimed without durable execution context. The native UI persists a pending client key/hash across lost acknowledgement and reload, requires explicit discard before replacing an uncertain payload and allows discard without dispatch, and targets regeneration deletion by immutable message identity; tests inject isolated app stores. Native UI Ask/Auto approval checkpoints now retain the admitted run identity; resume validates its exact scoped state/version and owned effective-security fingerprint before grants/dispatch, then submits the typed result to the same run. Root confirmation rejects changed mode/model snapshots. Public /v1 default/explicit Ask and explicit Auto now share scoped admission/CAS/submission with complete request/config/security fingerprints; no runtime_mode request inherits the previous Agent mode, and retries cannot redispatch. Other production entrypoints, durable continuation, result capture, acceptance/completion and recovery remain target.

Canonical server startup acquires an exclusive local TaskRunStore inode lease before opening the store and atomically marks admitted, running and submitted runs recovery_required. Competing startup fails before reconciliation. The lease covers HTTP loop and executor drain. Terminal runs and stored evidence are preserved. Resume, replay and external-effect reconciliation remain separate.

Trusted captured workspace_run persists confirmed atomic exchange and a separate cleanup warning in the same immutable row as process observation, bound to the original operation attempt. A scoped current-root marker can confirm publication across a process crash before the observation commit; missing or mismatched proof remains unknown. Read-only recovery projection does not settle external effects, transition the run or replay execution.

The browser recovery-evidence read checks the originating session and principal and requires recovery_required. A bounded snapshot projects recorded operation intents and optional observation metadata and verified submission identity. Raw output and producer text are withheld. No reconciliation, transition or replay is performed.

Initial browser Ask with a normally finished typed response, no tool calls, no web search and no pending approval uses scoped submission integrity validation. Acceptance and completion append separate versioned events in one transaction. Other runs, recovery and semantic final remain outside this slice.

Existing admitted UI/API Ask/Auto and captured approval continuation atomically bind an immutable scoped producer-report envelope to result_submitted history in the existing TaskRunStore. Exact v2-to-v3 additive upgrade preserves old identities/history with historical payload unavailable. CAS, rollback, scoped read, digest, size limits and HTTP projection/storage faults are tested. Producer text is not canonical tool capture, terminal acceptance or replay/recovery authority; sensitive nonterminal payload may remain indefinitely without GC.

Native Ask/Desktop/Auto approval continues the captured exact tool call and original history without user replay. Desktop retains a bounded host lease and thread-affine resources until resume or cleanup. Single-use state is principal/session-owned and volatile; missing/expired checkpoints fail closed. Local web search uses this same native loop; admission snapshots, HTTP cancellation settlement, original Ask finalization, compound once-scopes and UI history projection are covered. Auto preserves its original run frame, plan, start time and budgets; legacy auto.run replay is rejected. Canonical loop owns a volatile plan checkpoint preserving plan/task binding and completed steps; UI snapshots cannot claim completed execution. Once approval uses Gateway exact scope, pre-dispatch faults preserve pending state, and HTTP session grants roll back if resume did not start. Durable continuation, full canonical capture and payload storage remain target. Plan cancel clears the owned checkpoint and decision under the scoped lock; terminal projection faults fail the workflow without resurrecting the consumed decision. Initial pre-dispatch model conflict ends the owned task without dispatch. Retry checkpoints validate original lineage while executing their owned retry revision; fault settlement records the active attempt/task. Approval publication uses one UI storage write with rollback/cleanup on failure. Reject cleanup borrows the existing owner; scoped matching initial/resume cancellation signals before lock and preserves terminal results. Reject atomically commits terminal workflow and decision before checkpoint cleanup; storage failure preserves waiting state. Cancellation before first dispatch projects cancelled; shutdown timeout is diagnostic and does not interrupt remaining cleanup. Waiting-plan cancellation atomically commits workflow/decision removal before checkpoint cleanup. Cancelled workers preserve completed step results, available changes and counters. Scoped/static Agent retirement retains borrowers and locks after timeout; packet-thread cancellation drains before releasing ownership. Pending opaque tools do not acquire a durability/recovery guarantee.

Request-local typed Agent response reaches HTTP through sync return or ResponseProduced stream event. Auto outcome and returned Ask LLMResult/AgentToolLoopResult remain separate from text projection; post-result review/logging errors retain observations, explicit stream error/cancellation retains returned loop result, cancellation during dispatch captures completed ToolResult before stopping further calls and HTTP drains the typed observation without publishing cancelled content, provider creation/iteration exceptions retain completed observations through ToolLoopExecutionError, and ApprovalRequired reaches the existing outer approval handler. Missing/duplicate stream results fail without stale mutable result reads or execution rerun. Volatile boundary only: lifecycle authority, exceptional dispatch/serialization capture and canonical durability remain target. Full raw byte capture, durable continuation and full prior attempt history remain target. Desktop initial/resume responses retain the existing DesktopRunOutcome including verification and loop observations; presentation faults preserve it separately. No durable/canonical capture guarantee added.

Browser personal preferences are principal-scoped with subject-bound CAS, independent installation permissions, defaults for new principals and no import of global personal values; new browser model requests consume tone/instructions as user input without modifying system prompts or policy; tool continuations retain their original messages and Bearer requests use defaults.

Implicit UI configuration shapes consistently select local embeddings. Runtime model loads are cache-only, absent dependencies degrade Chat without remote fallback, local load can recover after files appear, explicit remote selection is preserved and existing vectors are not rebuilt.

A nonblocking browser notice explains unavailable local semantic search. Verified owner eligibility exposes explicit confirmed download, cached activation or retry through the existing endpoint. File presence and loaded weights are distinct; GET never initializes the runtime. Absent libraries get manual server guidance without fake installer or agent repair. Unknown diagnostics fail closed, Chat remains usable, and refreshed or unmounted observers ignore stale responses.

Owned session model changes reject active Chat/Plan and pending decisions until cancellation settles. Scoped execution locks cover model-bound decision creation, plan publication and project history/result publication. Approval steps enter waiting before decision visibility. Model revisions fence stale catalog and request snapshots; hydration cannot overwrite newer selection. UI manual and automatic restoration share generation/token ownership, preserving the current model request when New Chat fails.

Plan approve and execute require the displayed plan identity, hash and revision. UIHub atomically approves only the captured draft in Plan mode, rolls back storage failure and publishes after commit. Fresh execution validates the full binding; accepted idempotent replay retains its original binding during running revisions. Structured execution decisions capture and revalidate the full binding before execution or edits, rejecting replaced plans even at the same revision. Typed browser helpers take an explicit PlanEnvelope. Plan-card UI readiness is not claimed.

Canonical revisions fence late vector publication. Bound principal stores atomically delete exact canonical/atoms vector rows with bounded idempotency receipts on supported rollback-journal file DBs. Deprecated pins are excluded. Storage boundary only; browser API is tracked separately by memory.browser_management_api. No new model capability; Settings UI tracked separately. Encoding errors preserve prior vector and explicit partial-index save semantics.

Verified browser principal gets model/session-independent canonical pagination and exact-revision delete preview/explicit confirmation through an existing confirmed-only, non-model-exposed gateway tool. Bounded persisted opaque bindings survive restart; foreign/stale/expired/rebound operations fail closed, private responses are no-store and logs contain no Memory plaintext. Additive preferences_subject binds responses to the Settings account without changing Memory cursor subjects. UI tracked separately; auth tests use post-verifier identity fixtures, not deployed Access proof.

Settings reads paged owned canonical Memory independently of models/chats and previews one exact-revision deletion before explicit confirmation through the existing API. Account/operation/epoch fences reject mismatched and late responses; reopened panels wait for known confirmations before listing. No bulk wipe or false erasure claim. UI fixtures and temporary-store HTTP evidence do not establish deployed Access/provider behavior.

Owner Settings projects twelve configured ContextBudgetConfig values through a narrow separate read-only GET field and Advanced table. Member has no projection; writes to diagnostics or nested context_budget are rejected before settings mutation. No duplicated React defaults, per-field provenance, running Agent effective snapshot, token window or Auto enforcement claim. Existing inbox/embeddings Memory saves preserve the loaded ContextBudgetConfig; custom values survive fresh file reload and read view without enabling budget writes or member authority. No runtime consumer or concurrency guarantee change.

Verified auth metadata binds immutable browser subject context before bootstrap. Reachable last session/model/explorer/recent-root hints use explicit captured subjects; legacy values are not read/migrated and unavailable storage or subject disables persistence. Identity refresh is epoch fenced; subject changes remount private App, same-subject/transient failures preserve drafts, explicit denial removes App. No server auth authority change, instantaneous identity fencing or pending-send protocol claim; local/token tests do not re-enable legacy production auth.

Owner Settings exposes a separate read-only saved default model projection from the existing loader. Finite safe numerics, known enums, bools and null are sanitized; sensitive overrides expose presence only. Members omit diagnostics and POST is rejected. No React defaults, model probes, editor, active-chat capability or credential precedence claim. The separately adopted strict-bool loader prerequisite restores web_search_enabled; this read-only view reports the loaded request, not executed search or active-chat options.

Browser validates the existing owned session security snapshot before showing known policy/safe-mode or editable controls. Malformed, foreign, missing and failed reads remain unavailable. Epoch and conversation guards reject late read/save completions; reopening waits for known pending writes then reads, with no automatic POST retry. Save settlement separately refreshes the still-selected saved session summary even after the panel closes; other sessions are ignored. Existing explicit save and YOLO confirmations are preserved. No server authorization, grant provenance/revision/revoke, Desktop approval or instant identity fencing claim.

Owner Settings reads a narrow principal-bound saved Desktop rule projection through the existing shared store. Inspection never rewrites the rule file; existing runtime/list/mutation behavior is preserved. Sensitive command/description/ID/email/error contents are omitted; only known typed file-target tool/action roles expose paths, including separate download destinations. XPath/GUI/unknown targets and command/risk restrictions remain explicitly hidden. Captured-subject/epoch guards reject foreign and late responses; read failure is not an empty list, UI has no mutators. No new grant authority, revoke, effective-action permission, transient approval or host lease claim.

Owned session security GET captures saved policy and tool overrides under one existing UIHub lock, then projects known tool configuration sources from the same override map as displayed values. No session/grant writes or runtime consumer changes. Source labels describe configuration at refresh, including equal-value overrides and loader defaults; missing/invalid metadata and unsaved tool drafts remain unavailable. Existing session/epoch/save fencing preserved. No per-file default provenance, active-run capability, unified grant revision or revoke claim.

Existing owned session security POST validates all policy/tools input under the existing scoped agent lock before invoking either existing setter. Invalid combined requests cannot persist an earlier valid policy section. Owner/member ownership, YOLO confirmation, root constraints and valid update semantics remain unchanged. No new permission authority, API/schema, runtime consumers, CAS/revision or storage-failure transaction guarantee.

Saved session policy/raw tool overrides have a persisted revision and owned UIHub CAS. Trusted setters/import publish candidates after persistence; SQLite rejects stale snapshots inside the write transaction. Metadata initialization preserves configuration/messages. This is a storage prerequisite only: HTTP/UI preconditions remain unimplemented; installation defaults, grants, live revoke and multi-worker runtime are excluded. Existing startup-only principal normalization is revision-checked; NULL/blank principals restore to the configured owner, named principals cannot be reassigned and ordinary writers keep strict ownership checks.

Owned session security GET/POST expose saved-config revision and ETag from one captured snapshot. POST requires exact If-Match (428 missing, 400 malformed, 409 conflict), validates the full payload and existing root/YOLO guards under the scoped execution lock, then performs one persisted UIHub CAS. UI captures the selected-session revision; conflict requires a fresh read and another explicit save, with no automatic retry. Installation defaults, grants and running policy snapshots remain separate.

ModelConfig load preserves only JSON bool web_search_enabled; absent stays False and malformed non-bools raise without value echo. File reload/cold hydration and inert existing xAI request-path tests preserve session override precedence and distinguish saved configuration from active runtime. No new search executor, provider qualification, tools, grants, prompt strings, editor or live activation.

Owner-only no-store Settings snapshot projects existing server attachment validator constants; Developer displays items and Unicode code points per item/total without numeric React defaults. Member omits diagnostics, POST rejects before writes, malformed/missing metadata stays unavailable. No caps, parser, send, upload, model/provider capability or permission changes.

Owner-only no-store Settings projects existing short-term and summary input constants. Memory Advanced distinguishes transient user/assistant entries from saved-history summary messages and Unicode content slices, not retention, token window or remaining capacity. Member omits snapshot, POST rejects, missing/malformed values unavailable without React defaults. No Agent creation, summary generation, prompts, limits or Memory confirmation/lifecycle changes.

Owner-only no-store Settings snapshot allowlists numeric WebSearchConfig class defaults. Developer distinguishes candidate count, per-attempt timeout and content read budget from active tool/model state, result guarantees, total deadline and strict output size. Member omits snapshot, POST rejects, malformed values unavailable without React defaults. No tools/HTTP clients constructed, keys or provider exposed, capability probes, runtime/send/config/permission changes.

Owner-only no-store snapshot allowlists four numeric TtsConfig/SttConfig class defaults. Developer distinguishes Unicode text slices/per-attempt timeout and Agent STT from separate browser dictation. Member omits snapshot, POST rejects, malformed metadata unavailable without React defaults. New snapshot resolves no options/keys, constructs no tools/HTTP clients and runs no speech/capability request; existing env diagnostics, runtime, auth/approval and credentials unchanged.

Owner-only no-store snapshot allowlists two pure ShellConfig numeric defaults without loading policy, normalization, tools or subprocess. Developer distinguishes per-operation JSON overrides, subprocess timeout and post-capture Unicode truncation (combined ShellTool versus per-stream TerminalTool oneshot, markers extra) from PTY/Desktop, task deadlines, memory/output caps or effective grants/root/allowlist. Member omits metadata, POST rejects, malformed values unavailable without React defaults. Runtime and permission enforcement unchanged. I0 blocks Sandbox process execution before these configured limits are used; the read-only defaults snapshot is not execution readiness.

Owned no-store read projects numeric/enum/bool/null model options only from an existing paused approval continuation bound to current pending decision, session, identity and execution mode. GET creates no session/Agent/brain and resolves no model; no sensitive contents or fallback to defaults/main_config. Session Controls explicit read discards stale panel/session responses without writes. This is captured paused configuration, not general running state, permission, provider acceptance or resumability; capture/resume/cancel and persisted schemas unchanged.

After an attempted installation POST, HTTP/transport/unreadable-response failure discloses possible partial persistence and asks the user to check saved values before an explicit retry. Drafts survive, no automatic POST or false success callback; local validation and personal-only conflicts keep separate semantics. A readable Settings acknowledgement is required for installation confirmation and malformed bodies are not echoed. Existing server write order, role/policy, model/provider activation and transaction guarantees unchanged; exact applied fields remain unknown.

Default Sandbox tools, process verifier, manual terminal/Git/import and unqualified container commands refuse before host spawn/input. Explicit qualified rootless native workspace_run and the narrow staff process verifier (make check only, staged snapshot, no-publish) are the sole exceptions described in the same contract; neither can fall back to Host. Required process verification stays unavailable/error without a qualified command backend; process-free checks and explicit Desktop authority retain their boundaries.

Explicit pinned rootless Podman profile admits only native workspace_run through scoped Gateway and ComputerBackend. Principal-owned managed workspaces coordinate six writers, once approval binds immutable workspace/environment revision, finite explicit kernel tmpfs byte/inode slots bound active and retained private nofollow stages (one per principal), container logs are disabled, unknown mount ownership denies reuse, and bounded transfer plus atomic publication requires original content/revision after container settlement. Unknown/conflict stops subsequent tool/model calls without publication/replay. Raw bytes and actual exit exist internally; durable capture, run-intent fencing/recovery, other process consumers and production activation remain outside this partial slice. Unit tests do not independently prove OS isolation; real synthetic qualification evidence is recorded separately.

Narrow staff process verifier only: a separate pinned rootless Podman image with make (python:3.12.16-bookworm) admits exactly ["make", "-B", "-r", "-f", "Makefile", "check"] (-B forces the check recipe to run even when a file named check exists; -r disables the built-in rules, so no file can remake the trusted Makefile inside the stage via an implicit rule) on a staged snapshot of a managed workspace, with the same confinement as the qualified Python path and no publication back into the workspace. Execution requires a trusted WorkspaceBinding matching the run (principal/session/environment revision) and a qualified command profile; a Makefile alone grants nothing. The Makefile criterion hash is captured by trusted runner code before the loop and must match at verification time, otherwise ERROR verifier_criterion_changed. The criterion is read through a bounded no-follow read (O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, fstat identity check, 1 MiB cap); a present-but-rejected criterion fails with ERROR verifier_criterion_rejected, and a repository without a trusted criterion at run start carries the verification obligation in the run frame across resume, failing with canonical_repo_verifier_unavailable no matter which files appeared during the loop. Outcome mapping is finished+0 to PASSED, finished+nonzero to FAILED, unavailable/unknown/conflict to ERROR, never a faked PASSED; a cleanup failure after the check maps to ERROR (settlement_failed) with the known exit code preserved; after release the workspace is re-captured and compared with the verified snapshot, and a change during verification maps to conflict, never PASSED; an unavailable backend fails closed to FAILED_VERIFIER. Exact -r guarantee: only built-in rules are disabled. For arbitrary Makefiles with their own explicit self-rebuild rules or includes of agent-writable files this guarantee is insufficient and such a criterion needs separate review. Scope is E2E-fixture Makefiles only (no self-rebuild rules, no includes); full repository make check inside the sandbox, model shell tools and UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED semantics remain outside this slice. Unit tests do not independently prove OS isolation; real synthetic qualification evidence is recorded separately.

Only admitted synchronous Auto UI/API workspace_run and its captured native approval carry the original scoped run binding to the qualified rootless byte boundary. Existing guards precede durable operation intent, which is required before container start. Raw separate prefixes (1MiB/stream), observed counts/EOF, actual child exit or unknown, timeout/capture errors and digests commit atomically before opaque refs and bounded 32KiB UTF-8 views. Capture/store faults stop subsequent dispatch without replay; late historical observations cannot resurrect aborted runs. Additive Store v3-to-v4 preserves prior producer reports and history; sensitive raw bytes may remain indefinitely without aggregate DB quota or GC. Other tools/entrypoints, full canonical capture, acceptance and recovery remain target. Pytest stubs OS/engine boundaries; actual qualified synthetic evidence is separate.

Browser session lifecycle is owned by BrowserService (core/browser_service.py), not by DesktopBrowserTool: a BrowserProfile (profile_id + owner_id, default profile bound to the agent user_id in core/agent.py) keys one lazily created BrowserAutomationBackend, reused across operations and dropped on close, so the next operation starts a fresh session; profiles (and owners sharing a profile id) are isolated; close_all shuts every session down best-effort. DesktopBrowserTool is a thin adapter (request validation, cancellation, delegation, error mapping) and accepts an injectable service/profile so one service can be shared. All generic Playwright actions run unchanged through the service via the reused PlaywrightBrowserBackend. One active writer lease per profile since E02-T03 (core/browser_lease.py, wired into BrowserService for persistent backends): a second run gets profile_busy instead of a second Chromium on one user_data_dir, and a crashed holder is recoverable after profile health validation. Manual login handoff since E02-T04: login_handoff relaunches the same persistent profile headed under the held lease and pauses the run as WAITING_USER_INPUT / NEEDS_USER_AUTH; the run owner's one-shot Done resumes with a fresh observation (not proof of login), a 5-minute attempt timeout closes the window and requires an explicit retry, the lease is released only after a confirmed close, and password/OTP field values are masked before aria_snapshot so they never reach model messages, tool log or effect log. Effect classification since E02-T05 (core/browser_effects.py): observe/read operations are read, navigation is network, typing is a local draft mutation whose default is ask (browser_edit_requires_scope) since the scoped-authorization audit, submit/click/upload are external side effects that may require approval, download is a local write (destination path still classified separately), and unknown operations fail closed as external side effects instead of inheriting read. Secret boundary since E02-T07: the browser profile and lease storage roots are private runtime paths (shared/sandbox.py), so no workspace tool or workspace executor can read the profile path, a workspace root cannot be pointed at it, listing hides it, and a symlink from a workspace into the profile root is blocked (containment in workspace tools, O_NOFOLLOW refusal in managed capture). Persistence is real since E02-T02: one dedicated user_data_dir per (owner, profile) under ~/.local/state/slavikai/browser-profiles, started with launch_persistent_context, so cookies and local storage survive a browser restart (opt-in real-browser E2E); the directory is derived from profile identity only and validated under the dedicated root, so the owner's main Chrome profile can never be selected and no password database is ever copied. Scoped editing authorization since E02-T09: an approval for input/select can be scoped to one exact origin (scheme+hostname+port, no wildcard) and one run through the existing ToolGateway/DesktopPolicyRuntime; the trusted origin comes only from the live page (BrowserService.current_origin via page.url), never from model arguments, and is re-checked immediately before execution so a redirect or tab switch forces re-evaluation; a new run does not inherit the grant, persistent editing grants are refused, and concrete deny/ask rules stay above the grant. Structured browser postconditions since E02-T10: click/submit may declare browser_state {entity_id, selector, expect{kind: text|count, before?, after}} in their arguments; the tool captures the entity state before and after inside the same call (text: the status element inside the single element with that id, exact comparison, facts only — raw strings never enter result.data; count: the entity appearing 0 -> 1), polls within the call timeout with cancellation, and breaks capture on document navigation (performance.timeOrigin continuity token) or strict-masking pages; VerifierRuntime.verify_browser_postconditions confirms only when the capture proves the declared change (after matched, before did not), so an unconfirmed click/submit stays UNVERIFIED instead of DONE.

Owner Host Bridge daemon (E03-T02 + E03-T03, ADR-0013): AF_UNIX-only daemon (host_bridge/) listening on $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/slavikai/host-bridge.sock with a 0700 directory and a 0600 socket file, so a world-writable socket is impossible; refuses to start without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (no persistent fallback) and refuses a second instance on a live socket; authenticates every connection with SO_PEERCRED and accepts only the owner's UID before any protocol bytes are processed; serves only bridge.ping/bridge.version/bridge.capabilities. Protocol validation since E03-T03 (host_bridge/protocol.py): versioned request schema (version=1, required client-generated request_id echoed in every response, capability, optional principal_id/run_id attribution fields and params object), formal 64 KiB frame limit, deterministic typed rejections (malformed_request, unsupported_version, unknown_field, invalid_request_id, unknown_capability, frame_too_large), unknown top-level fields rejected rather than ignored so they can never become command arguments, and a per-request daemon deadline (request_timeout, handler abandoned and connection closed). principal_id/run_id are attribution/audit data only and never authorize anything (ADR-0013 §4); the out-of-band run-authorization mechanism is not part of T03. Runs as the owner's UID under a systemd user service (deploy/slavikai-host-bridge.service.example), never root, never sudo. Bounded host filesystem API since E03-T04 (host_bridge/fs.py): host.fs.stat/list/read/write/patch/move/delete/search addressed by root_id + relative path; roots from owner config (~/.config/slavikai/host-bridge.json, fail-closed, ADR §9 allowlist enforced after canonicalization: built-in workspace ~/.local/share/slavikai/host-workspace plus specific subdirectories of ~/Project, ~/Documents, ~/Downloads) or the built-in workspace root alone; bridge.capabilities returns roots as {id, mode} without host paths. Daemon-side path safety: canonicalize → containment → mode → write-exclusions (SlavikAI checkouts incl. structural detection, bridge launch files/config, policy store, ~/.local/state/slavikai — built-in even when config omits them) → DesktopPathSecurity classification with non-normal denied (ask maps to deny, /etc hard deny); operations are fd-relative with O_NOFOLLOW per component (symlink traversal and nested mounts forbidden in v1) so containment holds at operation time; move and recursive delete scan the whole subtree for protected descendants. Process capabilities since E03-T05 (host_bridge/process.py + host_bridge/spawn_helper.py): host.process.run/poll/kill run owner-approved command profiles only (typed slots path_in_root/enum/string/int; string only as data after '--' or as a '--flag=' value; profiles in the same host-bridge.json, same fail-closed loader; shells/setuid/non-ELF binaries and binaries inside allowed roots refused at load; capabilities expose profile id + slot names/kinds/required/enum values/int bounds only, never binary paths/argv/env/cwd). Enforcement per owner corrections: Landlock + NEWUSER|NEWNET|NEWIPC + NO_NEW_PRIVS + mandatory seccomp socket ban, metadata ban (chmod/chown/setxattr/utime, which Landlock does not restrict), and prlimit64 ban (a profile that knows the daemon/server PID could otherwise zero its RLIMIT_NOFILE), setpriority ban (same family: a profile could otherwise renice the daemon/server to 19 permanently), and sched_setscheduler/sched_setattr ban (same family: a profile could otherwise move the daemon/server to SCHED_IDLE and leave it starved under CPU contention after the profile ends), and sched_setaffinity ban (same family: a profile could otherwise pin the daemon/server to a busy CPU and leave it degraded after the profile ends), setxattrat/removexattrat ban (same family as the metadata ban: the classic setxattr ban does not close these new at-variant syscalls, and a profile could otherwise set a POSIX ACL on a file it cannot read and lock the daemon/server out of its own config), and ioprio_set ban (same family: a profile could otherwise move the daemon/server to IOPRIO_CLASS_IDLE and leave it starved under disk contention after the profile ends), and MAKE_FIFO/MAKE_CHAR/MAKE_BLOCK/MAKE_SOCK in the Landlock handled mask with no allowing grant (unlisted handled rights are allowed by default, so mkfifo/mknod are refused everywhere, inside an allowed root or outside it), applied by the trampoline helper (never preexec_fn from the multithreaded daemon); helper closes service/inherited FDs, writes the child's uid/gid maps itself (self-write is denied by AppArmor's unprivileged_userns profile), and execs the approved binary identity-bound via execve of /proc/self/fd/<fd> on the open fd (execveat is not used: it breaks uutils multicall binaries on this host, which see the fd number as the utility name); Landlock grants only explicitly allowed parts of the tree, each bound to the (dev, ino) the daemon recorded and opened by the helper without following any symlink component, so a replaced object fails the spawn instead of granting the replacement (every directory gets directory-operations-only rights and every allowed file its own rule, so a protected file nested inside an allowed root stays denied and a file created under a granted directory after the walk stays unreadable and unwritable to a long-lived profile — directory rules never carry file-content rights; symlinks and nested mounts (including same-device bind mounts, checked against the real mount topology) never granted); a directory that is an ancestor of a protected subtree (write-excluded, checkout, or deny-classified) gets only the non-mutating "rdir" grant (READ_DIR + REFER) instead of "dir": Landlock rules union within one ruleset, so a mutating grant on an ancestor would otherwise hand REMOVE_FILE/REMOVE_DIR/MAKE_* to the protected subtree — verified live that a profile cannot delete or create inside an excluded subdirectory or checkout while listdir/traversal and legitimate operations in allowed siblings still work (direct create in the cwd itself is refused once the cwd is such an ancestor); env is a minimal fixed set plus profile literals (LD_PRELOAD/PYTHONPATH and friends forbidden); stdin /dev/null. One cgroup v2 scope per process_id (systemd-run --user --scope -p Delegate=yes) is the tree kill: placement precedes exec, final status only after the cgroup is empty AND the scope leader is reaped, kill deadline expiry returns 'killing' and the reaper completes; PDEATHSIG is extra protection for the direct child. A startup probe through the same spawner in the daemon's real context verifies actual TCP/UDP/pathname-socket refusal, metadata-operation refusal, foreign-pid prlimit refusal, foreign-pid setpriority refusal, foreign-pid scheduler-policy (sched_setscheduler/sched_setattr) refusal, foreign-pid CPU-affinity (sched_setaffinity) refusal, foreign-path setxattrat/removexattrat refusal, foreign-pid I/O-priority (ioprio_set) refusal, SysV shared-memory attach (shmat) refusal (own IPC namespace: the owner's segments do not exist for the target), mkfifo refusal, late-created-file refusal (a file created in the cwd after the grants were installed stays unreadable/unwritable), protected-file refusal, allowed-file read, uid mapping and scope placement; the cwd itself must classify "normal" before any grant is computed (a protected cwd such as "credentials" gets no grant even when its children classify normal); if the helper dies after the target started but before its first status.json, the record stays under reaper control — the tree is destroyed and the record finalizes only once the cgroup is confirmed empty, never on leader death alone; the same holds after any exception once a handle exists (e.g. a SIGTERM send timing out while the spawn deadline expires): the record stays in cleanup state until the tree is destroyed and the cgroup is confirmed empty, never finalizing on the error alone; every status publication bumps a generation counter, and a poll accepts a tail + counters snapshot only when the generation did not change across the read, so a 256 KiB tail rotation can never hand new bytes out at old absolute offsets; every status publication also carries the SHA-256 of each tail's exact bytes, and a poll accepts a snapshot only when the tails hash to the published digests as well, so a tail flushed between the two status reads (generation still old, counters still old) can never hand new bytes out at old offsets — and a poll that cannot read a consistent snapshot after 10 attempts fails typed (snapshot_inconsistent) when the last snapshot is a torn rotation instead of returning torn bytes (a small tail newer than its counters is pure growth and still clamps as before); a poll answers only from a frozen snapshot of the verified counters + tails captured before the check, so a concurrent refresh (another poll, the reaper) cannot move the counters under a verified tail; if the scope path cannot be resolved at spawn, the tree is destroyed by unit name and the scope confirmed gone before the spawn fails, so a helper that already forked descendants cannot outlive the failed spawn; the grant walk checks the entry limit and the cancellation token per entry as the iterator is read, so a huge directory cannot exhaust the daemon's memory before either fires; probe failure hides the process capabilities from bridge.capabilities and makes a direct run answer process_unavailable. Spawn is idempotent per request_id (retry returns the same process_id, no second process; cancel+launch is one committed state transition); running is returned only after enforcement + exec are confirmed; poll is instant, UTF-8 with replacement decoded incrementally, so an invalid byte earlier in a chunk cannot consume a following incomplete multibyte suffix (the suffix is held back and completes on the next poll); a live stream that published only the first byte of a multibyte character answers an empty chunk at the same offset instead of failing the poll, and only a max_bytes that cuts an already-available character fails typed (invalid_params), absolute offsets + retained_from, 256 KiB tail per stream, frame-budget chunking; global cap 4 running, finished records kept 10 min with a separate cap of 32; 120 s process cap enforced by the daemon reaper (tree kill on timeout). Before the reaper starts a timeout termination it checks natural completion first (as _kill() does), so a process that exits just before its deadline keeps its published exited result and exit code instead of being rewritten to timeout. Accepted limits of the directory-operations-only grant model (verified live): a new file created directly in the cwd tree can be created (empty) but not written or read — new content goes in $TMPDIR and is hard-linked into the tree, which keeps it writable via the tmp path and visible to the owner in the tree; and an atomic tmp+rename update of a granted file lands but the new inode is not covered by the inode-bound file rule, so the updated file is unreadable/unwritable to the profile afterwards (in-place writes to granted files still work). The design that would remove both limits — an isolated filesystem view (mount namespace + bind mounts of only the granted files) — is a design decision for the owner, not part of this ticket. Run-scoped STOP and process ownership since E03-T06 (host_bridge/process.py, host_bridge/daemon.py): every process record carries the (principal_id, run_id) binding fixed at commit time from the request envelope; host.process.stop kills only the non-final processes bound to one (principal_id, run_id) pair under a single shared deadline of min(token, 4.0 s), returns the processes with their final states plus all_final (true only when every listed process reached a final state within the window; an unknown run is a successful empty answer); a run that was stopped refuses new commits with run_stopped; a spawn in flight across a stop is destroyed at the adoption point and finalizes as spawn_failed once the cgroup is confirmed empty, never as killed; a retry with the same request_id but a different binding is rejected with binding_mismatch; a repeat stop never moves the original kill deadline, re-signals, or overwrites an existing kill reason; stopped-run marks are dropped when the last record bound to the run is swept, and expire after 600 s when no record exists; unbound processes are never touched by stop; normal run completion does not stop processes. At daemon startup the orphan sweep kills leftover slavikai-bridge-<namespace>-*.scope units of this daemon's own socket directory (the namespace is the socket dir's hash, so a second daemon with another socket directory never loses its scopes to this sweep) and stale run dirs (no adoption); any sweep error raises BridgeConfigError and the daemon exits 2. Exclusive daemon ownership is held for the daemon's whole lifetime by an flock(2) lock file in the socket directory, taken before any socket probing, so the bind->listen window is closed and a second daemon can never mistake the first's live socket for stale; the lock file is never unlinked. Fork 6 residual risk stays documented: kill/poll/stop are unauthenticated daemon-side and rely on the server to enforce ownership; the out-of-band run-authorization mechanism (ADR-0013 §4) remains open. Diagnostic sources are deadline-bounded (systemctl 2 s, disk under a shared 2 s budget with concurrent probes) so a hung source can never push the handler past the per-request deadline; process_list trims oldest-first under the 64 KiB frame budget with count keeping the total and truncated marking the trim. The diag capabilities are always visible in bridge.capabilities — unlike the process capabilities, which hide when the enforcement probe fails — so the diagnosis answers exactly when the diagnosed subsystem is broken. Read-only by construction: no writes, no process spawn except the read-only systemctl --user show query, verified by tests asserting absence of mutation. Server-side ownership policy for process_list (global diagnostics only for a trusted context) is a T11 adoption obligation (ROADMAP.md §E03-T11). Status stays partial until T11 (bridge E2E).
